normal.description: Baseline physiological variability and sensor noise.

hypoxia_drop.description: SpO2 falls linearly to a target and stays there.

motion_low_perfusion.description: Motion and low perfusion flag unreliable readings.

finger_out.description: Oximeter reports unavailable values and an unattached sensor.

disconnect_mid_reading.description: The link drops after the configured notification count.

low_battery.description: A low battery report precedes power loss.

out_of_range.description: Wire-valid readings exceed plausible device ranges.

frozen_sensor.description: Measurement payloads freeze, including device timestamps, while notifications continue.

malformed_packet.description: One notification loses its final byte before normal frames resume.

provenance.note: AGENTS.md section 4 requires simulated twins to cover frozen or stuck sensor faults. Index 2 is a zero-based scenario choice, not physiology or a clinical threshold. Each characteristic retains its own last measurement bytes, including its device timestamp; battery events are unchanged. Non-NASA: this fault-injection index does not describe a physiological quantity.
82: below the 95 to 100 percent of 'most healthy individuals', C08 (FDA). Scenario value, not a clinical threshold.
2: puts the reading at about 39 C, above 'A high temperature is usually considered to be 38C or above', RT30 (NHS, in docs/product/ROUTINE.md). Scenario value.
165 and 105: above 'If your blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg or higher, you have Stage 2 high blood pressure', RT27 (MedlinePlus). Scenario value.
Values outside any plausible device or physiological range (SpO2 above 100 percent is impossible by definition). Scenario values.

Fault behaviors required by AGENTS.md section 4 (motion, low signal, disconnect, out of range); status bits from the Bluetooth SIG GATT Specification Supplement (non-NASA: no NASA catalog document defines a device protocol). Counts are scenario values.
